logout_redis_behavior.redis_available: Existing Supabase local signOut succeeds and clears session; logout does not query Redis.
logout_redis_behavior.redis_unavailable: Timeout, unavailable/invalid Redis response or missing Redis configuration does not prevent logout; no Redis-generated 503 or details returned.

checkout.order_creation: New authenticated checkout_submit_order wraps existing trusted order insertion and snapshots; ownership remains enforced.
checkout.duplicate_checkout_idempotency: Synchronous client lock; SHA-256 input fingerprint plus UUID in memory/sessionStorage; database key(customer_id,request_id) returns original order for identical payload and rejects changed payload. Different IDs/tabs remain distinct purchases.
checkout.inventory_checks: Active category/product/variant and stock validated under product/variant locks. No reservation/decrement; cumulative pending orders can exceed inventory.
checkout.completion: Only successful persisted response clears cart and pushes /order-confirmation/[orderId], then refreshes. Failed request preserves cart/form; notification timeouts can delay success response.

rate_limiting.backend: Upstash-compatible HTTPS Redis REST with atomic Lua INCR/EXPIRE/TTL; private PostgreSQL budgets for selected direct writes/RPCs.

thresholds.scope: proxy mutations except dedicated POST /auth/logout without next-action

protected_endpoints_actions: Proxy POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE excluding Next static/image matcher paths
rate_limiting.development_fallback: In-memory expiring counters only when not NODE_ENV=production and not VERCEL=1 with incomplete Redis settings.
rate_limiting.redis_outage: Four-second Redis timeout; invalid/missing configuration or bad response yields 503/action error. Proxy limit exhaustion yields 429 with Retry-After. Dedicated logout is exempt and never contacts Redis.
rate_limiting.ordinary_browsing: GET/HEAD page reads do not invoke Redis; cart/wishlist POST-based reads can degrade while pages remain available.
rate_limiting.shared_ip: Proxy/IP budgets are shared by NAT users; missing trusted Vercel IP falls into unknown bucket; non-Vercel host uses shared local identity.
rate_limiting.privacy: HMAC identities in expiring Redis keys, namespace VERCEL_ENV or NODE_ENV; raw IP/email not stored in limiter keys.
rate_limiting.database_limitations: Budgets roll back with failed transactions; invalid direct RPC abuse still needs provider protections. Admin/null-auth bypass applies to customer-write trigger, not all budgets.
rate_limiting.customer_error_transport: Proxy returns HTTP status; caught Server Action failures use normal action-result messages, not necessarily HTTP 429.
rate_limiting.logout_exception: Only POST /auth/logout without a next-action header skips proxy Redis budgets, after Origin/content/size validation. It dispatches only logout. The logout function retains assertSameOrigin and existing Supabase signOut but has no Redis call. Other methods, paths and Server Action requests remain fail-closed.

manual_smoke_tests: 1. Create isolated staging Supabase and Redis; confirm no production database, provider recipients or credentials are connected.
2. Verify existing migration sequence, capture function/ACL/RLS/promo backups and take a recoverable database snapshot.
3. Run promo preflight SQL; stop on any would_violate_constraint=true and approve unpaid/cancelled promo consumption policy.
4. Configure exact staging SITE_URL, Supabase URL/public key, Redis URL/token/HMAC and Supabase callback allowlist; keep sandbox disabled for real unpaid-order tests.
5. Apply existing prerequisite migrations only to a fresh staging project, then the security migration once; run supabase/verify-security.sql and require all checks true.
6. Build/deploy isolated Preview under separate authorization; verify canonical, deployment and branch-origin requests work and foreign/missing Origin mutations fail.
7. Register/confirm two test customers; login, refresh account, logout, request/reset password; inspect secure cookie persistence and safe redirects.
8. Confirm customer cannot access admin pages/actions, other customer orders/addresses, private tables, privileged notification RPCs or payment/price writes.
9. Add quantity 2 or 3 of an available variant; inspect cart subtotal, promo discount, configured shipping and final total.
10. Submit unpaid order; verify exact snapshots, pending/unfulfilled state, one order, success-only cart clear and confirmation/history ownership.
11. Retry same request ID after simulated lost response; verify same order and one promo use. Changed payload with same ID must fail.
12. Test insufficient stock, expired/exhausted promo, invalid fields and backend failure; preserve cart/customer fields. Test concurrent last-use promo submissions.
13. Exercise product/variant/category/inventory/promo/shipping/image/fulfillment/return admin forms and stale-version conflicts.

14. Test Redis shared budgets, NAT/shared-IP behavior, 429 Retry-After and outage/recovery. Login/checkout/admin/cart must remain fail-closed, ordinary GET pages remain available, and dedicated POST logout must succeed without Redis while foreign/cross-site logout fails.
15. Verify desktop/mobile navigation, both logos, cart drawer, consented GA/Meta and client navigation with no unexpected CSP violations or secret-bearing client chunks.
16. Configure test email/SMS recipients; verify backend claim and single delivery, pending events without providers and manual reconciliation of interrupted/failed sends.
17. Rehearse rollback with a post-migration order; preserve orders/usage, restore saved function bodies and ACLs, then previous code; verify auth/admin/checkout.
18. Record hosted results and assess rendering latency/cost before requesting production approval.

compatibility_steps: Drop five newly added triggers under maintenance
Restore seven replaced function bodies from pre-migration captures
Restore captured ACLs for all eight affected existing functions, including legacy checkout
Revoke customer/public/anon execution on new checkout_submit_order
Keep added private tables/outbox columns and newly accepted orders intact
Retain/reconcile promo usage if post-migration orders exist

rollback_plan.function_backup_method: Before migration export pg_get_functiondef(oid), function identity, owner and proacl for each listed public function. Legacy checkout body is unchanged but its ACL must be captured.
rollback_plan.acl_grant_backup: Capture actual explicit and default-expanded grants, including PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, service_role and any custom roles. Restore function bodies before former customer notification grants; never grant customers access to the new backend-only bodies.
rollback_plan.rls_backup: Capture relrowsecurity/relforcerowsecurity and policies for private.checkout_settings and affected tables. Compatibility rollback may leave added restrictive RLS; exact reversal must use actual prior state.
rollback_plan.promo_counter_backup: Export public.promo_codes id,code,used_count,max_uses,updated_at and record cutover time; keep snapshot outside repository. Do not blindly restore if new orders accepted.
known_rollback_limitations: New orders must be preserved; full database restore can lose post-cutover activity
Exact old counts/timestamps cannot be inferred after migration without backup
Compatibility rollback leaves additive schema and private records
Dropping new tables would discard idempotency data
Old application/functions restore earlier security weaknesses
Notification sends cannot be undone by SQL
Migration cannot simply be rerun after partial manual rollback
